assertions.text: Multiple @TableTest methods each addressing a distinct concern
assertions.evidence: Methods include calculatesBaseRateByZoneAndWeight, appliesDimensionalWeightWhenGreaterThanActual, appliesOversizeSurchargeWhenAnyDimensionExceedsLimit, carrierDoesNotAffectPrice, etc., each a separate @TableTest.

assertions.text: Do not fragment a single concern across multiple same-fixture tables
assertions.evidence: Surcharges concern split into 5 separate tables (oversize, fragile, insurance, hazmat, combinesSurchargesInOrder) all fixed to 'EU standard, weight fixed to 3.0kg (base rate 7.50)'.

assertions.text: Cell values make the rule falsifiable, not merely distinguishable
assertions.evidence: Most tables (e.g. calculatesBaseRateByZoneAndWeight rows 5.00,7.50,12.50,20.00,8.00,12.00,7.00,30.00) vary distinctly; only carrierDoesNotAffectPrice has one row by design to prove invariance.

assertions.text: A reader can state the rule from the table alone
assertions.evidence: Descriptions state base rates and thresholds e.g. 'oversize dimension threshold (100)' and 'Premium is 0.6% of insured value, with a $3.00 minimum'; other deltas derivable from stated base rate 7.50 and total cost columns.

assertions.text: Parameter types match calculateShippingCost signature
assertions.evidence: 'void calculatesBaseRateByZoneAndWeight(String region, String speed, double weight, BigDecimal baseRate)' and 'List<Integer> dimensions' plus 'assertEquals(0, expected.compareTo(actual), ...)'.

assertions.text: Scenario names describe conditions, not outcomes or generic labels
assertions.evidence: Scenario names like 'EU standard, light', 'Large package, dimensional weight used', 'At the size limit', 'Same zone and weight, any carrier'.

assertions.evidence: Question-mark columns: Base Rate?, Rate?, Total Cost?, Total Cost?, Total Cost?, Total Cost?, Total Cost?, Total Cost?

assertions.text: Column names use domain language, not code identifiers
assertions.evidence: Column headers: 'Region | Speed | Weight | Base Rate?', 'Dimensions | Rate?', 'Insured Value | Total Cost?', 'Carrier | Total Cost?'.

assertions.evidence: First table uses 'Base Rate?', second table (same computed base-rate quantity) uses 'Rate?', and all later tables use 'Total Cost?' for the same computed cost.

assertions.text: Read the class's test titles as the sorted index a reader would scan, stripped of their tables.
assertions.evidence: Method names: calculatesBaseRateByZoneAndWeight, appliesDimensionalWeightWhenGreaterThanActual, appliesFragileSurcharge, appliesHazmatHandlingFee, combinesSurchargesInOrder, carrierDoesNotAffectPrice — mostly verb-first active phrasing with subject early, no generic 'should/test/verify' prefix repeated 3+ times.

assertions.text: Each @TableTest has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules.
assertions.evidence: e.g. appliesOversizeSurchargeWhenAnyDimensionExceedsLimit has just 2 rows ('At the size limit' / 'Just over the limit'), appliesInsurancePremiumWithMinimum has 4 rows covering none/below/at/above — no redundant permutations within any single table.
